common_name: Golden Mop Cypress (Threadleaf Mounding Gold Falsecypress)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; some afternoon shade helps prevent foliage bronzing in intense summer heat, though full sun gives the brightest gold color.

directions: Golden Mop is a dwarf, mounding false cypress selected for stringy, thread-like sprays of bright golden-yellow foliage that spill over themselves in an informal, tousled mound, distinct from the finer, more upright Gold Thread Cypress. It stays low and rounded for many years, needs essentially no pruning, and provides year-round texture and color contrast against darker evergreens or as a rock garden and foundation accent. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the brightest gold color, though a little afternoon shade helps in the hottest climates; established plants are low-maintenance but resent soggy, poorly drained soil, which promotes root rot.

common_name: Techny Arborvitae (Broad Pyramidal Winter-Hardy Green Arborvitae)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, spacing for a hedge if a screen is wanted; Techny holds its deep green color through winter better than many arborvitae cultivars, which tend to bronze in cold weather.

directions: Techny is a broad, dense, pyramidal arborvitae grown for its reliable deep green color that holds through winter cold far better than many other Thuja occidentalis selections, which often bronze or yellow in freezing weather. Its wider, fuller pyramidal shape makes it a substantial specimen or privacy screen, slower-growing and more compact than towering cultivars like Green Giant, and it needs only light shearing, if any, to maintain a tidy form. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; arborvitae generally performs best in cooler climates and struggles with the intense heat and humidity of the Deep South, so it is best suited to the northern edge of its range.

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Rheingold's warm golden-bronze color deepens through fall and winter and is most vivid with full sun exposure.

directions: Rheingold is a slow-growing, dwarf, rounded-to-conical arborvitae valued for foliage color that shifts through the seasons, emerging soft yellow-gold in spring, deepening to a rich old-gold through summer, and warming further to coppery bronze in fall and winter cold. Its compact form and long season of changing color make it a favorite specimen for rock gardens, mixed conifer beds, and foundation plantings where a small, slow-growing accent with year-round interest is wanted. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the best color development; like other arborvitae it prefers cooler climates and is not well suited to the extreme heat and humidity of the Deep South.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; like other junipers, Grey Owl will not tolerate wet feet and needs sharp drainage to avoid root and crown rot.

directions: Grey Owl is a wide-spreading, arching juniper selected for silvery gray-green foliage, taking on soft purplish-bronze tones in winter cold, on a low, informal, fountain-shaped mound that works well cascading over a wall or covering a slope. It is derived from eastern red cedar and shares that species' remarkable adaptability, tolerating heat, drought, poor soil, salt spray, and the humidity of the Gulf South better than many other juniper cultivars bred from less heat-tolerant species. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; established plants need little care beyond occasional shaping to control the spreading habit, and good air circulation helps avoid the fungal blights that can affect junipers in humid climates.

common_name: Sea Green Juniper (Arching Fountain-Form Bright Green Juniper)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; sharp drainage is essential, since junipers decline quickly in soggy or heavy clay soil.

directions: Sea Green is a vigorous, arching juniper with bright green, fountain-shaped sprays of foliage that curve outward and downward in a graceful vase form, distinct from the flatter, more prostrate habit of many spreading juniper cultivars. Its bright, clean green color and fine texture make it a versatile foundation or mass-planting shrub, and it holds up well to the summer heat and humidity of the Gulf South, provided drainage is sharp. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, and prune only to remove wayward branches, since its natural arching form is part of its appeal; avoid overhead watering late in the day to reduce the risk of foliage blight in humid weather.
